extracted.intended_audience: USPTO policymakers, patent practitioners, antitrust enforcers, and other patent policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A federal agency comment on the USPTO's proposed rulemaking about terminal disclaimer practice to obviate nonstatutory double patenting, assessing anticompetitive harms and recommending rule features to limit strategic use of disclaimers that create patent thickets. Focuses on effects in pharmaceuticals/biologics and broader competition policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic function of a terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer is a binding stipulation by a patent applicant that the patent’s term will not extend beyond the term of another patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by applicants to overcome USPTO rejections for nonstatutory (obviousness-type) double patenting; while it prevents term extension beyond the original patent, it can still expedite issuance of patents with duplicative claims that entrants must overcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting standard (when to reject claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonstatutory double patenting rejection is appropriate where conflicting claims are not identical, but at least one examined application claim is not patentably distinct from the reference claim(s) because the examined claim is either anticipated by, or would have been obvious over, the reference claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounded in the judicially created doctrine to prevent unjustified timewise extension of the right to exclude; used to reject claims that are essentially the same as those in a prior patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed enforceability condition for terminal disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposed rule, terminal disclaimers made to overcome a nonstatutory double patenting rejection would have to include a provision that the patent would be enforceable only if it has not been tied by a terminal disclaimer (to obviate nonstatutory double patenting) to another patent containing any claim that has been finally held unpatentable or invalid by a federal court or the USPTO, and for which all appeal rights have been exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition would mean that patents tied together by terminal disclaimers 'stand or fall together,' so invalidating the original claim would render later-filed patents with terminal disclaimers unenforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: whether terminal disclaimers facilitate patent thickets
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminal disclaimers can expedite issuance of patents with duplicative claims and facilitate the growth of patent thickets by allowing applicants to quickly add more patents that fence off existing technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate portfolios for duplicative claims linked by terminal disclaimers (e.g., Humira portfolio where many patents were duplicative and linked). Such linkage increases costs for entrants who must challenge multiple patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticompetitive impact metric: effect on market entry for generics/biosimilars
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent thickets and terminal-disclaimer-linked patents can delay and frustrate entry of new biosimilars and generic drugs, increasing prescription drug costs and limiting patient access to affordable options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider empirical indicators such as the prevalence of follow-on patents in Orange Book listings, litigation patterns, and spikes in terminal-disclaimer filings near expiration of exclusivity periods as evidence of exclusionary strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of strategic behavior: timing and prevalence of terminal-disclaimer filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies found filing of patents with terminal disclaimers spiked near the end of FDA-granted exclusivity for branded biologics, and many litigated Orange Book patents are follow-on patents relying heavily on terminal disclaimers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use timing (e.g., filings near exclusivity expiration), percentage of duplicative patents in a portfolio, and presence of terminal disclaimers as indicia of strategic anti-competitive behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement/harm metric: cost burden on challengers
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenging patents is costly: the average cost to challenge a patent in inter partes review or post-grant review is estimated at $774,000, and litigating a patent case in federal court can cost considerably more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing rules or conduct, account for these litigation and administrative costs as a barrier that patent thickets amplify for potential market entrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary patents concern (follow-on patents reliability and impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary patents obtained after the initial patent (frequently included in patent thickets) tend to be more frequently invalidated but can still delay generic or biosimilar competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory or examination practices should consider that even if secondary patents are weaker, their existence can impose delay and cost; reducing their proliferative use (including via terminal disclaimers) can improve market entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper Orange Book listing as an anticompetitive criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper listing of patents in the FDA’s Orange Book can harm drug competition and has been the subject of FTC challenges and litigation; many litigated Orange Book patents are follow-on patents not directed to new chemical entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize Orange Book listings for improper or 'junk' patents and consider delisting or other remedies as part of reducing the exclusionary effects of patent thickets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy balance criterion: reform should reduce gamesmanship while preserving alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule should reduce incentives for incumbents to file numerous duplicative patents tied by terminal disclaimers without foreclosing legitimate alternatives for applicants to address nonstatutory double patenting rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reforms (like enforceability-conditioning disclaimers) to lower strategic filing while leaving in place reasonable options for patent owners to address legitimate claim-differentiation issues.
